I've noticed this quirk since I joined a few months ago. It's not technically a bug since it does what it was told to do: when you vote, the number changes to how many upvotes or downvotes it has, according to whether you up- or downvoted. I wouldn't say this is a desirable feature; I'd rather it display the point sum of the post, instead.

Well, it doesn't look very logical to me - before you upvote, it does show the point sum, and after an upvote the score changes by 2 points. So the same place is used to show two different things (score / upvotes).
Yes, I was making a point that I didn't like it. Looking for the total score of a post can only be done by manually calculating the sum of upvotes and downvotes, which I found annoying.

This is not a bug. The same label is used to display 3 different types of information:

  • current score (upvotes-downvotes) (if you did not vote)
  • upvotes (if you upvoted)
  • downvotes (if you downvoted)

I agree that it is not very logical, but current design does not allow for 3 different labels between the voting arrows. To avoid confusion, I guess we could stop displaying the number of downvotes or upvotes and only show the score (in frontpage mode) but I am quite sure that there would be other people who are strongly against this.
Ok, this is a feature, but I don't see why the total number of upvotes (or downvotes) is important - the ranking uses score after all.
Good question. I guess we can ask the users what they want to see (if/when we have a slightly bigger user base) and opt for the most desired way of displaying this data.
